newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA BANCOREX TAKES INTEREST RATES HIGHER AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA BANCOREX TAKES INTEREST RATES HIGHER AGAIN.

text.p: Romania's state-owned bank Bancorex on Monday has raised interest rates on leu deposits -- the third rise since the start of the year -- in line with tough monetary policies aimed at curbing inflation.

A Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA statement said the bank's annual rate on one-month deposits were up 35 points to 120 percent, while the two-month rate had risen to 125 percent from a previous 85. Three-month deposits now bear an annual 130 percent, up from 80 percent.
Bancorex's six- and nine-month rates as well as rates on one-year deposits went up by 20 points to 100 percent yearly.
Sight rates remained unchanged at an annual 40 percent.

Most banks have increased leu deposit rates since early 1997, in line with tighter central bank monetary policies, which triggered an upswing in the one-week refinancing rate to 226.35 percent last week from 125.45 percent.

Romania's year-on-year inflation quickened to 56.9 percent last year from 27.8 percent in 1995 and is forecasted to jump to 89.5 percent this year, led by January's fuel price rise and February's liberalisation of electicity and food prices.
